text: Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size hidden layer called a "reservoir," which is typically sparsely connected. The weights of the reservoir are usually set randomly during training and remain fixed. Training involves adjusting only the readout weights that map the reservoir's state to the desired output. Reservoirs are trained by exposing them to input data, allowing them to learn the dynamics of the system without direct weight tuning.
